findings.issue: In the expanded order, none of the four Metz omissions has a rubric. The two Tair conditionals have neither a tei:note child nor @type, so under 'How an undecided scope is set off' they count as processor directions. With metz undefined, Tair prints plainly and nothing tells the reader it is omitted in Metz. The canonical Kol conditional is type="marked" but also has no note, so the expanded output prints brackets with no explanation. The Frankfurt omission, by contrast, has an editorial rubric at :1603. JLPTEI-3 says that when opensiddur:rite is unset, variants are kept 'together with the heading that says whose custom it is'. Selection itself works correctly when metz is set.
findings.recommendation: Follow the Frankfurt pattern. Give each expanded Tair conditional an editorial tei:note type="instruction" child (for example בק״ק מיץ אין אומרים). For the two expanded Kol transclusions, wrap each in an index-level metz=false conditional with the same note. The outer conditional is redundant with the inner marked one, but that is harmless. This keeps the documentary instruction out of the reusable stanza, as the user intended. Not blocking for draft structure.

findings.issue: Three native rubrics say when text is or is not said, but each is encoded as a free-standing tei:note type="instruction" outside the j:conditional it governs: the Frankfurt direction (:373), the Metz Tair rubric (:390) and the Metz Kol rubric (:460). JLPTEI-3 (Instructions; Kinds of rubric) says such a rubric is the conditional's own note and is printed only while the condition is undefined. As encoded, all three print in every compiled documentary edition, including when frankfurt_am_main or metz is decided. Because :390 sits before the weekday shabbat=false block, the Metz Tair rubric also prints on Shabbat, when Tair is not said. The Kol rubric at :460 is correctly inside the shabbat=true block and is printed only once. That placement does keep it off the second occurrence, as the human wanted. I accept this as a deliberate documentary-preservation choice.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for a draft structure. Later, either make each rubric the tei:note child of its documentary-index conditional (:375, :402, and a new index-level metz conditional around the :461 transclusion), or record in the encoding notes that native conditional rubrics are kept as unconditional directives in the documentary order. If the first option is chosen, move :390 inside the weekday block.

findings.issue: The Kalir attribution 'חתום בראשי חרוזים אלעזר בירבי קליר.' (tei:note type="description") is inside the weekday conditional but outside the Metz Tair conditional (:402-412). In a metz=true... correction: in a metz=false-evaluating Metz edition, Tair drops out and the attribution for its acrostic still prints with no poem in front of it. Under 'Kinds of rubric', a description belongs to the passage it describes and is left out with it. I did not check whether tair_vetaria.xml also carries this attribution internally.
findings.recommendation: Move :414 inside documentary_metz_tair_vetaria_source_he, after the transclusion and before its endConditional. Alternatively, make it part of the Tair unit's own scope.

findings.issue: Attah Hu is nested inside two conditionals with the identical test frankfurt_am_main=false. The outer one carries the rubric 'חוץ מפרנקפורט אם מיין / Outside Frankfurt am Main'. The inner one has no rubric and contains the ark open/close actions and the poem. Both are balanced and the result is correct. The rubric's sense (said outside Frankfurt, therefore omitted in Frankfurt) agrees with the human's confirmation. No German skip direction remains in the expanded output.
findings.recommendation: No change needed. The inner wrapper could be dropped later to simplify.

findings.issue: The rubric 'ע״ס א״ב.' appears twice. In aafir_nezer.xml it is at div level before the part_1 milestone, so it is outside the part_1 range, and only the expanded whole-poem transclusion (:1678) reaches it. The documentary index has its own copy at :524. So it is printed once in each order and never twice. This is consistent, but the same source rubric is stored twice.
findings.recommendation: Record which copy is the source-attributed one in the encoding notes. No structural change needed.
